title: provider-auth -01: §13.2 replay names keyMaterial; SHOULD nonce on consumable requests
description: §13.2 says replay is mostly harmless because MIMI requests are idempotent or carry MLS messages a hub rejects twice. keyMaterial is neither: each answer hands out a KeyPackage, so a replay within the created window consumes one (Haven saw over the hackathon weekend how fast users run out). In -01: §13.2 names keyMaterial and any other request whose answer hands out something that runs out; signers SHOULD include the RFC 9421 nonce parameter on those requests; verifiers SHOULD reject a repeated nonce from the same key within the created window. Resolve the Open Issues bullet 'whether nonces should be required' accordingly (required in effect where replay costs something, optional elsewhere). Also update §5.2/§5.3 to mention nonce for these requests. mimid: sign keyMaterial with a nonce; track nonces per keyid for the window on the verifier. Source: Jason Bolduc's review on mimi@ietf.org, 15 Nov 2026 (Message-ID CA+7d1z=LQ+iuYYum-z-SUssV8X5PJgeZL7EW5R2f0Jd4FkzTvA@mail.gmail.com); Mark committed to it publicly in his reply of 16 Nov (IETF notes/2026-11-16-mimi-provider-auth-jason-reply-sent.md). Draft source: ~/PROJECT/ietf-mimi-provider-auth/draft-atwood-mimi-provider-auth.md.
